So online shops have many advantages:

-fewer expenses (less employees, no physical building to buy and maintain, etc)

-most online purchases are tax-free, it is unlikely most of the things you buy will ship from in-state. Brick and mortar stores still charge sales tax.

-no need to physically leave your house to buy things

So the question is, will we still have brick and mortar shops in the future? Where I live at least, electronics often cost more than double in the store what they cost online. Though food is still expensive to ship so we may still have physical stores for that at least. And I don't think I've ever seen a local best buy with more than 2 customers in the whole store.
Future of brick and mortar shops?
I don't think bars will be going anywhere any time soon.
Bars and restaurants are more for the social experience and not having to cook. I'm talking about stores.

High end clothing stores won't be going anywhere. People aren't going to buy suits online, they're going to want to go in the store, try it on, see how it fits. This goes the same with cosmetic stores, they're going to want to know how something looks or smells before they buy it.

Pet stores would be an exception as well, as you can't buy animals and have them delivered to you.

People aren't going to buy suits online,

Like the fuck I wont. They are working on being able to get your dimensions from a web-cam and custom tailor suits. If they can get it in a reasonable price point I'd buy a ton of them.

Yes, but the types of brick and mortar stores will change. We will start to see electronic stores go away. But, we will still see some clothing stores stick around. At least, until returns of online purchases becomes easier. Also, there will always be stores for home repairs like a Lowes or Home Depot and even auto parts stores. There's a lot of last minute things that people will need to get. Screwing in the drain plug to your car and the head snaps off and it's sunday so the deal is closed? Auto parts store. Putting up plywood in your home and run out of nails? Lowes.

Basically, as long as there will be last minute shoppers, there will be brick and mortar stores.

I think we will have physical stores for several more generations. Right now I know 40 years old that refuse to buy online and only buy from physical locations.

To get to an all online system you are going to have to have much better overall internet speed, much better and faster shipping to all parts of the world, and far more computer security and identity security
Internet speed nowadays is more than good enough. Your cc can be just as easily stolen by hackers in a physical store (remember the target thing?).
Its not the actuality of the security but the perception. People fifty plus don't trust online shopping, I read a poll somewhere, I'll try to dig it up.
You still need buildings to store product. Amazon doesn't just imagine things into being at your door step.
